newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends at session lows, origins noted.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends at session lows, origins noted.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Thursday at the day's lows after a rangebound session marked by origin selling and roaster buying on the dips, traders said.

But little immediate reaction was felt after reports Colombian exporters have had to reshedule this month's coffee shipments because of leftist guerrilla attacks and highway blockades across the country.
"If exporters declared force majeure in Colombia, then futures might jump," said one trader, adding that the news had so far had little effect on prices.
Benchmark November robusta coffee futures ended the session on Thursday down $16 at $1,508 a tonne.
Turnover on the exchange reached 2,595 lots.
A meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) on Friday will keep traders interested, but little of substance is expected.
"We will be keeping an eye on it, but nothing major is expected," said one.
"They could always say something to spark the market into life," said another, but said it was unlikely.
Technically, some traders said London futures were attempting to consolidate after recent losses.
November futures slid to a low of $1,471 last week from a high of $1,740 on August 27, sending the contract into what chartists called oversold levels.
The contract could extend its gains, said chartists, but it will need to do more work to reach the $1,600 peak area last seen in early September.
